comparisons.peer_summary: USPB comprises Branded Cards (with proprietary and co-branded portfolios), Retail Services (with co-brand and private label relationships), and Retail Banking (providing traditional banking services to retail and small business customers).
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup disclose the structural composition of their co-branded credit card programs within their respective platform or segment definitions. Goldman Sachs identifies the 'GM credit card program' as part of 'Platform Solutions' and tracks the specific asset classification of these co-branded portfolio assets (held for sale). Similarly, Citigroup defines its 'USPB' segment to include 'Branded Cards' which explicitly comprises 'proprietary and co-branded portfolios' as well as Retail Services with 'co-brand and private label relationships'. While GS focuses on the transient status of a specific partner's assets (GM), C provides the broader taxonomy of how co-branded assets are organized within its reporting segments.

sentences.text: During 2024, in connection with the planned transition of the GM credit card program to another issuer, the firm classified the GM credit card program (within Platform Solutions) as held for sale.
As of December 2024, the assets related to the GM credit card program consisted of the GM co-branded credit card portfolio of $1.8 billion (included in loans).

USPB includes Branded Cards and Retail Services, which have proprietary card portfolios and co-branded card portfolios within Branded Cards, and co-brand and private label relationships within Retail Services.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm holds exclusive rights to issue and market co-branded credit card products through contractual agreements with numerous partners lasting five to ten years, who provide customer lists and endorse the programs.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the nature of co-brand credit card partnerships and the rights associated with them. Goldman Sachs describes the transition of the 'GM credit card program,' implying a structured partnership where assets are classified and eventually sold to another issuer. Citigroup discloses its contractual framework with co-brand partners, noting that these agreements grant the firm 'exclusive rights to issue and market co-branded credit card products' and specify that partners 'endorse the co-brand credit card programs and provide their customer or member lists.' Both firms treat co-branded cards as distinct strategic assets governed by specific partner agreements, rather than solely as proprietary portfolio items.
